docs.title: Wally
docs.text:
Wally is a low-latency, lock-free Java library that implements a hybrid Write-Ahead Log and Event Queue entirely in off-heap memory, backed by memory-mapped files.

Standard Java queues (ArrayBlockingQueue, ConcurrentLinkedQueue) suffer from lock contention and GC pressure from per-message allocations. Wally avoids both:

  • Off-heap: records live in mmap'd segment files accessed through the Java FFM API (MemorySegment).
  • Lock-free hot path: producers claim space with a single atomic fetch-add; readers use acquire/release ordering.
  • Zero allocation in steady state: flyweights and callback-based reads, so no per-message objects.
  • Hybrid: one append-only log serves as a durable WAL (flush policies, crash recovery, checkpoints) and as an event queue (named consumer cursors, retention).

Status

Pre-alpha. The MVP is being built. See the Roadmap.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
• Harness: JMH for throughput; a fixed-rate driver + HdrHistogram for latency, to avoid coordinated omission.
  • Scenarios: 1P1C and NP1C (N = 1, 2, 4, 8); payloads 32 B, 256 B, 4 KB; flush policies none, periodic(1ms/5ms), sync.
  • Baselines: ArrayBlockingQueue, JCTools MPSC, LMAX Disruptor, Chronicle Queue.
  • Allocation: JMH -prof gc (gc.alloc.rate.norm) and an Epsilon GC run.
  • Environment: record CPU, kernel, JDK, JVM flags, core pinning. Publish raw data and the script that produced it.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text: ./gradlew :wally-bench:jmh -Pjmh.profilers=gc

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Draft

Filled in as milestones land.

Term Meaning Log Append-only sequence of records spread across fixed-size segment files. Position 64-bit logical byte address of a record: segmentIndex * segmentSize + offset. Monotonic, never reused. Segment One pre-sized, memory-mapped file (%020d.wly). Starts with a 64 B header. Record 16 B header + payload, 8 B aligned. length == 0 means not yet committed. Claim / commit Two-phase write: reserve space, write the payload in place, publish by writing length with release semantics. Appender Per-thread write handle. Reuses one Claim flyweight. Tailer Read handle. Polls records via a callback (segment, offset, length, position). Consumer group Named tailer whose position is persisted in the cursor file. Flush policy When page-cache data is forced to disk: none, periodic, sync. Flushed position Highest position guaranteed durable under the current flush policy. Checkpoint WAL-mode marker: everything below it may be deleted. Retention Deletes segments wholly below the minimum of all group cursors and the checkpoint.

docs.title: File format
docs.text:
Draft

Finalized in M1. All integers are little-endian. Format version: 1.

docs.title: Segment file
docs.text: Name: %020d.wly (segment index, zero-padded). Size: fixed segmentSize (power of two).

docs.title: Segment header (64 B)
docs.text: Offset Size Field 0 6 magic WALLY\0 6 2 format version 8 8 segment size 16 8 base position (segmentIndex * segmentSize) 24 36 reserved (zero) 60 4 CRC32C of bytes 0–59

docs.title: Record (starts at a multiple of 8)
docs.text:
Offset Size Field 0 4 length: payload bytes; 0 = uncommitted. Written last, with release semantics. 4 2 type: 1 = DATA, 2 = PADDING 6 2 flags 8 4 CRC32C of the payload (0 when ChecksumMode.NONE) 12 4 reserved 16 length payload — 0–7 alignment padding to the next multiple of 8

A PADDING record fills the remainder of a segment when the next record doesn't fit.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
Draft

Finalized and verified in M3.

docs.title: Durability per flush policy
docs.text:
Policy Survives process crash Survives OS crash / power loss Cost none() Yes, once committed (page cache) No guarantee Lowest latency periodic(d) Yes Records at or below flushedPosition(); up to d of data may be lost Group commit sync() Yes Yes, once append returns One force() per append

macOS

msync/fsync on macOS does not guarantee data reaches stable storage. True durability needs F_FULLFSYNC. Treat macOS as a development platform.

docs.title: Visibility and ordering
docs.text:
• A record is visible to tailers once its length is published with release semantics.
  • Tailers see records in position order. They never skip an uncommitted record; they wait at it.
  • With multiple producers, position order is claim order, not commit order.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text: On open, Wally scans from the last checkpoint and truncates at the first uncommitted or CRC-invalid record. Recovery never surfaces a corrupt record.

docs.title: Roadmap: MVP (M0–M4)
docs.text:
Target: JDK 25 LTS (final FFM API), Gradle Kotlin DSL, zero runtime dependencies in wally-core.

flowchart LR
  M0[M0 memory layer] --> M1[M1 mmap segments] --> M2[M2 MPSC] --> M3[M3 durability + recovery] --> M4[M4 consumer groups + retention]

docs.title: M0: memory layer + in-memory log
docs.text:
• Mem (static aligned VarHandles: plain, acquire/release, getAndAdd, CAS) and PaddedCounter (value isolated by 128 B padding).
  • RecordFormat: int length | short type | short flags | int crc | int reserved (16 B header, 8 B alignment). length == 0 means uncommitted. TYPE_PADDING fills the end of a segment.
  • Single-writer append/poll over one Arena.ofShared().allocate(size, 4096) segment.
  • Read API: RecordHandler.onRecord(MemorySegment seg, long offset, int length, long position), so there are no slices.
  • JMH 1P1C vs ArrayBlockingQueue (payloads 32 B, 256 B, 4 KB).

Exit: unit tests pass; JMH -prof gc shows gc.alloc.rate.norm ≈ 0; Epsilon GC test passes (-XX:+UseEpsilonGC -Xmx64m, 50M records).

docs.title: M1: mmap'd segments, single writer
docs.text:
• 64 B segment header: magic WALLY\0, format version, segment size, base position, header CRC.
  • SegmentFile maps with FileChannel.map(READ_WRITE, 0, size, arena). Unmap is arena.close(), gated by a refcount.
  • Position = segmentIndex * segmentSize + offset (ADR 0002).
  • Rollover writes PADDING, then maps the next segment. A Preallocator agent creates and pre-touches segment N+1.
  • Appender.append(...) and tryClaim(len) → reused Claim flyweight (segment(), offset(), commit(), abort()).
  • ChecksumMode {NONE, CRC32C}. Risk: java.util.zip.CRC32C over asByteBuffer() may allocate; fall back to a slice-by-8 implementation reading from the MemorySegment.

Exit: jqwik model test (random append/poll/reopen/segment sizes vs ArrayList oracle) passes; rollover tested at exact boundaries; File format written.

docs.title: M2: multi-producer claim/commit
docs.text:
• Tail claim with getAndAdd (ADR 0004). The claimant whose range covers the end of a segment writes padding and triggers the roll; claimants landing past the end retry.
  • Commit: payload first, then setRelease(length). Reader: getAcquire(length) (ADR 0003).
  • producerMode(SINGLE | MULTI). Single mode uses a plain store.
  • jcstress (commit visibility, no torn header/payload) and Lincheck (MPSC append + tailer).
  • JMH NP1C (N = 1, 2, 4, 8) with HdrHistogram and a fixed-rate driver.

Exit: no forbidden jcstress outcomes; Lincheck passes; still zero allocation.

docs.title: M3: durability + crash recovery
docs.text:
• FlushPolicy.none() | periodic(Duration) | sync(). Periodic = flusher agent force()s dirty ranges (group commit).
  • Appender.flushedPosition() exposes the durable watermark.
  • Recovery on open: validate headers → scan from checkpoint → stop at first zero length / bad CRC → zero the tail.
  • Crash harness: child JVM appends with sync() and reports acked positions; parent kill -9s it at random times, reopens, and asserts the prefix property.
  • Corruption tests: random byte flips and truncation.

Exit: 1,000 crash iterations green locally and in Linux CI; Guarantees written.

docs.title: M4: consumer groups + retention
docs.text:
• CursorFile: small mmap'd file with fixed slots (name hash + 64 B name + padded position).
  • wal.tailer("group") resumes from the persisted cursor; commit(), seek(position). Ad-hoc wal.tailerFrom(position) is not persisted.
  • Retention agent deletes segments wholly below min(group cursors, checkpoint) after the refcount drains.
  • RetentionPolicy.wal() (truncate on checkpoint(position)) vs RetentionPolicy.queue(maxSegments) (appender returns BACK_PRESSURED).
  • WaitStrategy: busy-spin / yield / park.
  • Examples: event-sourcing journal, inter-thread pipeline.

Exit: model test extended with groups, restart and retention; 30-minute soak shows no fd or mapping leaks; Concepts and quickstart docs complete.

docs.title: Out of scope for MVP
docs.text: CLI tools, SBE codec, Micrometer metrics, cross-process IPC, stuck-producer unblocker, LazyFS power-loss tests, Jazzer fuzzing, Maven Central publishing.

docs.title: Verification commands
docs.text: Command Checks ./gradlew build Unit, jqwik and Lincheck tests ./gradlew :wally-stress:jcstress Memory ordering ./gradlew :wally-core:crashTest kill -9 recovery harness ./gradlew :wally-bench:jmh -Pjmh.profilers=gc gc.alloc.rate.norm ≈ 0 ./gradlew :wally-core:epsilonTest Zero allocation under Epsilon GC mkdocs serve Docs render locally

docs.title: ADR 0001: Use the FFM API instead of Unsafe
docs.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-05

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Wally needs off-heap memory, memory-mapped files, atomic operations on raw memory, and deterministic unmapping. Historically this meant sun.misc.Unsafe + MappedByteBuffer.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Target JDK 25 LTS and use the final Foreign Function & Memory API: MemorySegment, Arena, ValueLayout.varHandle() for atomics, FileChannel.map(..., arena) for mapping, and Linker for madvise.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• + Supported API: Unsafe memory access warns from JDK 24 and is slated for removal.
  • + arena.close() unmaps deterministically. No more relying on GC to unmap.
  • + Bounds and liveness checks, which the JIT removes on hot paths.
  • − Requires JDK 22+ (we pick 25 LTS). Excludes users stuck on 17/21.
  • − asSlice() allocates, so the API exposes (segment, offset, length) triples.
  • − Closing a shared arena while another thread is using it throws, so segment lifetime needs refcounting.

docs.title: ADR 0002: Address records by logical byte position
docs.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-05

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Consumers and checkpoints need a stable, seekable identifier for a record. Options: a sequence number (needs an index file) or a byte position.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Identify records by a 64-bit logical position = segmentIndex * segmentSize + offsetInSegment. segmentSize is a power of two and fixed per log.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• + O(1) seek: segmentIndex = pos >>> log2(segmentSize), offset = pos & (segmentSize - 1). No index file.
  • + The tail counter, cursors and checkpoints are all plain longs, so they are cheap to CAS and persist.
  • − Positions are not dense: users can't compute "the Nth record". A sparse sequence index can come later if needed.
  • − Segment size can't change for an existing log.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Two-phase claim/commit with length as the commit marker
docs.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-05

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Producers must write records in place (zero copy) while readers scan concurrently, without locks. Readers must never observe a partially written record.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Claim: reserve align8(16 + len) bytes at the tail. The length field is still 0.
  2. Write: fill type, flags, CRC and payload with plain stores.
  3. Commit: store length with setRelease.

Readers load length with getAcquire. 0 means "not committed", so stop. A positive value guarantees the rest of the record is visible (release/acquire happens-before).

Segments are zero-filled on creation, so unwritten space always reads as length == 0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• + One release store per record; no locks, no CAS on the read path.
  • + Torn writes after a crash show up as length == 0 or a CRC mismatch, which makes recovery simple.
  • − A producer that dies between claim and commit leaves a hole that blocks readers. Mitigation (post-MVP): an unblocker that pads over holes after a timeout.
  • − Max payload is bounded by int and by segment size minus headers.

docs.title: ADR 0004: Claim tail space with fetch-add, not a CAS loop
docs.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-05

docs.title: Context
docs.text: In multi-producer mode, producers contend on the tail counter. A CAS loop retries under contention; fetch-add (LOCK XADD on x86, LDADD on ARMv8.1+) always succeeds in one instruction.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Producers claim with getAndAdd(tail, recordLength). If the returned range crosses the segment end:

  • The claimant whose range covers the segment end writes a PADDING record from its start to the end, then triggers the roll.
  • Claimants whose range starts at or past the end don't write anything. They wait for the next segment to become active and retry there.

Single-producer mode skips the atomic and uses a plain store plus release.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• + Wait-free claim in the common case; throughput scales better than a CAS loop under contention.
  • − The tail can overshoot the segment end, so the logical tail must be re-based on roll. This needs careful jcstress coverage.
  • − Overshooting claimants waste a small amount of address space (no disk space).

docs.title: 0. Core idea
docs.text:
Build one thing: an append-only log addressed by position. Both modes sit on top of it:

  • WAL = log + durability policy + crash recovery + truncation at checkpoints.
  • Event queue = log + named consumer cursors + retention (delete a segment once every cursor has passed it).

Prior art worth studying: Agrona and Aeron (log buffers), Chronicle Queue, the LMAX Disruptor.

Foundational decision: use the Java 22+ FFM API (MemorySegment, Arena, VarHandle) instead of sun.misc.Unsafe. See ADR 0001.

  • JDK 24+ warns on Unsafe memory access, and it is headed for removal.
  • FileChannel.map(mode, off, size, arena) gives deterministic unmapping with arena.close(). That fixes the old MappedByteBuffer unmap problem.
  • Linker allows calling madvise/mlock without JNI.

docs.title: 1. Problems to solve
docs.text:
# Problem Approach 1 Record framing 8-byte aligned header: int length, short type, short flags, int crc32c, then the payload. Little-endian, fixed. A PADDING record type fills the rest of a segment. 2 Atomic publish Two-phase claim/commit. A producer reserves space, writes the payload, then writes length last with setRelease. Readers getAcquire the length; 0 means "not committed yet, stop here." 3 Multi-producer contention getAndAdd on the tail counter (fetch-add, not a CAS loop, so there are no retries). 128-byte padding around hot counters to avoid false sharing. Single-writer first, then MPSC. 4 Segment rollover Fixed-size segment files (e.g. 1 GiB). The producer whose claim crosses the boundary writes the padding and triggers the roll; other producers retry. Logical position is segmentIdx * segSize + offset, so seeking is O(1) with no index file. 5 Page-fault stalls A background thread pre-allocates and pre-touches the next segment, plus madvise(SEQUENTIAL/WILLNEED). Document THP and vm.dirty_* tuning. 6 Durability mmap writes only reach the page cache. Flush policies NONE, PERIODIC (group commit every N ms) and SYNC, via MemorySegment.force(). macOS needs F_FULLFSYNC for real durability. Document what "acknowledged" means for each policy. 7 Crash recovery On open, scan forward from the last checkpoint and validate each CRC. Truncate at the first torn or zero frame. File header: magic + format version + segment size. 8 Stuck producer (hole) A producer thread that dies between claim and commit blocks readers forever. Fix (post-MVP): after a timeout, an "unblocker" writes padding over the hole (as Aeron does). 9 Segment lifetime vs. readers Closing a shared Arena while a reader is using it throws. Reference counting or epoch-based reclamation before unmapping or deleting. 10 Zero allocation MemorySegment.asSlice() allocates. Expose (segment, offset, length) instead of slices. Reused flyweights, non-capturing or pre-allocated handlers, return codes instead of exceptions. No iterators, boxing or varargs on the hot path. 11 Backpressure / waiting WaitStrategy: busy-spin, then Thread.onSpinWait, then yield, then park. Queue mode returns BACK_PRESSURED when retention would be exceeded. 12 Cross-process (post-MVP) Shared mmap'd metadata file holding the tail and cursors. Aligned CAS on mapped memory works across processes.

State the claims precisely

  • "Zero-allocation" means steady state on the hot path.
  • "Lock-free" means the append and read paths; fsync is not lock-free.

docs.title: 2. Code organization
docs.text:
Gradle multi-module build. Core has no runtime dependencies. JPMS module-info exports only io.wally.api.

wally/
├─ wally-core/        # io.wally.api              public: Wally, Appender, Claim, Tailer, configs
│                     # io.wally.internal.memory  FFM, VarHandles, alignment, native madvise
│                     # io.wally.internal.log     framing, appender, reader
│                     # io.wally.internal.segment mapping, rolling, preallocation, refcount
│                     # io.wally.internal.recovery scan, CRC verify, truncate
│                     # io.wally.internal.concurrent padded counters, wait strategies, agents
│                     # io.wally.internal.queue   consumer groups, cursors, retention
├─ wally-bench/       # JMH
├─ wally-stress/      # jcstress + Lincheck
├─ wally-examples/    # event-sourcing journal, inter-thread pipeline
├─ docs/              # this site + ADRs
│  (post-MVP)
├─ wally-codec-sbe/   # optional SBE integration
├─ wally-metrics/     # optional Micrometer binding
└─ wally-tools/       # CLI: dump / verify / recover / stats

docs.title: API shape (sketch)
docs.text:
try (Wally wal = Wally.builder().dir(p).segmentSize(1 << 30)
        .flush(FlushPolicy.periodic(Duration.ofMillis(5))).open()) {
    Appender a = wal.appender();                  // one per thread, reused
    long pos = a.append(src, off, len);           // copy path
    Claim c = a.tryClaim(64);                     // zero-copy path, reused flyweight
    if (c != null) { c.segment().set(JAVA_LONG, c.offset(), 42L); c.commit(); }

    Tailer t = wal.tailer("billing");             // named, persisted cursor
    t.poll((seg, off, len, position) -> { ... }, 256);
}

Methods return long positions, with negative constants for BACK_PRESSURED, ROLLING and CLOSED (the Aeron style).

docs.title: 3. Patterns
docs.text:
• Flyweight: Claim and record views over raw memory, with no per-message objects.
  • Two-phase claim/commit: the publish protocol.
  • Single Writer Principle: the default mode. MPSC is opt-in.
  • Sequence/cursor (Disruptor): consumers are just positions.
  • Strategy: WaitStrategy, FlushPolicy, RetentionPolicy.
  • Builder + immutable config.
  • Agent / duty cycle (Agrona): background flusher, preallocator and retention cleaner on one optional thread.
  • ADRs: every non-obvious decision is recorded in docs/adr/.

docs.title: 4. Utility
docs.text:
• Target use cases, each shipped as an example: event-sourcing journal, local durable outbox in front of Kafka, inter-thread pipeline, replication log for a KV store.
  • Zero dependencies in core, published to Maven Central.
  • Explicit guarantees table: what survives a process crash vs. a power loss under each FlushPolicy. See Guarantees.
  • CLI tooling to inspect and repair files.
  • Stability: file-format versioning, API compatibility checks with japicmp, semver.
  • Honest benchmarks against ArrayBlockingQueue, JCTools MPSC, Disruptor and Chronicle Queue, with reproducible scripts.

docs.text: Layer Tool What it covers Unit JUnit 5 Framing, alignment, padding, rollover at exact boundaries, CRC Model-based jqwik Random append/poll/roll/reopen sequences checked against an ArrayList oracle Memory ordering jcstress Claim → commit → read visibility; no torn length/payload observed Linearizability Lincheck MPSC append + concurrent tailers Crash Child JVM + kill -9 mid-write, then reopen Prefix property: every durable-acknowledged record is present and no corrupt record is surfaced Power loss LazyFS (FUSE that drops unsynced writes), Linux CI Validates FlushPolicy guarantees for real Corruption Jazzer fuzzing of the recovery scanner; random byte flips and truncation Recovery never crashes or returns garbage Soak Multi-hour run with rollover + retention Leaks, file-descriptor growth, mapping leaks

docs.title: Non-functional
docs.text:
• Throughput and latency: JMH across 1P1C and NP1C, payloads from 32 B to 4 KB. HdrHistogram with a fixed-rate load generator so coordinated omission doesn't hide tail latency. Report p50/p99/p99.99/max.
  • Zero-allocation proof:
    • JMH -prof gc: assert gc.alloc.rate.norm == 0.
    • Steady-state run under -XX:+UseEpsilonGC with a small heap. Any allocation eventually exhausts the heap and fails the run.
    • JFR allocation events as a cross-check.
  • Profiling: async-profiler and JMH -prof perfasm.
  • Durability cost: throughput vs. flush interval curve.
  • Environment: real numbers on dedicated Linux with pinned cores and isolcpus. CI perf checks only as coarse regression gates.
  • Matrix: JDK 25 LTS × Linux x86/ARM × macOS.
